title: Move/copy/retain/block classification
description:
Implement the pure edge-aware classifier over inventory and recursively discovered edges. Complete repository-wide ownership using every issue-linked working-tree document's supported embedded closure, apply per-reference selection, compute mirrored destinations under `<archive_root>/<container-short-id>/<repository-relative-source>` for containers (user-visible surfaces use short hashes; an existing container directory whose hidden ownership marker names a different container blocks as a target-level destination conflict, and a markerless directory blocks when it holds unaccounted entries), and classify each working-tree artifact as move, copy, retain, or block from needs-destination and needs-source. Apply archive-root precedence before managed-path classification, component-aware managed/permanent policy, pinned historical behavior, symlink blocking, and normative missing-source evaluation. Evidence such as permanent, outside-owner, active-owner, unmanaged-path, and archived-source is not itself a blocker; blockers are structural.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Ownership includes supported embedded references reachable from every issue-linked working-tree document repository-wide and marks outside-subtree owners.
- [hard] REQ-02: Classification follows the edge-aware calculus deterministically: shared active/outside/permanent consumers force source retention; a relatively referenced dependency copies when its relocated parent needs it at the mirror and otherwise retains; a successful pin adds no working-tree constraint while failed commit reads block.
- [hard] REQ-03: Every supported edge's relative or root-relative resolution mode affects the action, and no emitted layout leaves a relocated parent's supported edge unresolved; an archive-root dependency reached relatively from a relocated parent is copied to the current mirror while its original is retained.
- [hard] REQ-04: Managed, permanent, and archive-root checks use normalized path-component containment, so `dev/active-other` never matches `dev/active`.
- [hard] REQ-05: An unmanaged selected root blocks with `unmanaged-selected-root`; an unmanaged embedded dependency carries `unmanaged-path`, always needs source, copies only when it also needs destination, otherwise retains, and never moves.
- [hard] REQ-06: Destinations mirror full repository-relative source paths beneath the destination root, use the container short-id segment derived from the container's own id prefix, and keep identical filenames in different directories distinct; an existing directory whose ownership marker names a different container blocks as a destination conflict.
- [hard] REQ-07: A differing-content occupied destination blocks as `destination-conflict`; a content-identical one classifies `already_archived` with publication skipped (adoption-by-content), while its action and any source deletion still follow the calculus and the execution-time deletion precondition; symlink roots, targets, or traversals block as `symlink-artifact`.
- [hard] REQ-08: Archive-root containment is evaluated first for every path; it produces `archived-source` evidence and needs-source, bypasses `unmanaged-selected-root`, retains direct roots with null destination and no relink, copies relative-edge dependencies only when a relocated parent needs the mirror, and never moves or deletes the archived source.
- [hard] REQ-09: `reference_changes` is exact per reference: pinned references never relink; a container selects only unpinned terminal-inside references; a document selects all unpinned direct owners only after all direct and embedded owners are terminal; every unselected unpinned reference forces needs-source, and move occurs only when no source constraint remains.
- [hard] REQ-10: A working-tree root absent at both its stated path and computed mirror destination blocks with `missing-source`; a missing embedded target emits `missing-edge-target` on the referencing artifact, adds no needs-destination constraint, is excluded from before/after edge validation, and does not block the target.
